findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The page explains why it is about firstmate rather than Athena, so the newcomer is not confused about the change of subject.
findings.source: A study is Athena's written reading of another software project, taken at one fixed commit ... Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it

findings.text: The first section after the header is a failed placeholder. The newcomer's first chance to see Athena's promised models, verdict and cost on a real job shows only an error.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv.

findings.text: A link meant for the page's owner sits in the header, where a first-time visitor will wonder whether it is meant for them.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: The next step is concrete: prerequisites, clone, install and a first command, linked from the top of the page.
findings.source: Next steps: Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm ... Install Athena from the checkout: ./setup.sh ... athena ask "add a changelog"

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed study of firstmate's internals (exit codes, places, guard conditions). A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to read a lot of material about another project.
findings.source: Transitions (t1 to t12 cards), e.g. "the spawn is deferred with exit 75 and the item stays queued"

findings.text: Several terms used throughout the page are admitted to be undefined, so some sentences stay unclear even after checking the glossary.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." / "does not define an endpoint" / "does not define a heartbeat" / "does not define a wake"

findings.text: This frank note may make a newcomer doubt how thorough Athena's reading is, which works against the page's purpose of showing that it can explain an unfamiliar project.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths ... none was run, so no run confirmed that a script behaves as its header says."

findings.text: The footer section refers to an internal folder the newcomer cannot see, which does nothing for that reader.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
